title: GPU prewarming experiment — regional capacity sync (2026-03-16)
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures the notes and outcomes from the cross-region sync on the GPU prewarming experiment (pilot), regional capacity observations for the last sprint, and proposed follow-ups. Intended audience: infra on-call, platform capacity owners, SRE, and product operations who consume capacity guarantees.

Meeting context and attendees:
- Date: 2026-03-16 10:00 PT (30m)
- Attendees: Maya Patel (owner), Ethan Romero, Sofia Li, Rajesh Kumar, Lina Torres, Quentin (SRE on-call, joined for 10m)
- Objective: review prewarming pilot telemetry, validate hypothesis about reduced cold-start tail latency and improved steady-state utilization, decide whether to expand to eu-west and ap-south next week.

Quick summary / TL;DR:
- Prewarming experiment (us-west-2) ran for 72 hours. Results: 32% reduction in cold-start latency P95 for small-burst workloads, 11% increase in average GPU utilization during prewarm windows, cost delta +4% (due to idle prewarm capacity).
- Observed fast degradation of benefit when prefix caching TTL < 15m; recommend default prewarm TTL = 20m for now.
- No major stability incidents. One thermal-throttle alert on node gpu-uw2-34 triggered a temporary shift of warm slots; SRE patched fan control and raised monitoring threshold.
- Decision: expand pilot to eu-west-1 only (staged rollout) on 2026-03-19; delay ap-south until we have a cheaper prewarm profile and tighter cost guardrails.

Detailed experiment notes:
- Hypothesis: proactively starting containers/instances and warming model KV cache before expected traffic spikes will reduce request tail latency without materially increasing cost if prewarm windows are targeted.
- Setup: 40 prewarm slots (A100-80GB equiv) in us-west-2, tied to traffic prediction from historical hourly model and a lightweight predictor (exposed as /predict-prewarm). Prewarm TTLs tested: 5m, 15m, 20m, 60m.
- Metrics collected: cold-start latency P50/P95, token-generation latency, GPU utilization, prewarm slot idle time, billing delta (approx).
- Results table (aggregated):
  - TTL 5m: P95 cold-start reduction 10%, GPU util +3%, cost +1.5%
  - TTL 15m: P95 cold-start reduction 25%, GPU util +7%, cost +3%
  - TTL 20m: P95 cold-start reduction 32%, GPU util +11%, cost +4%
  - TTL 60m: P95 cold-start reduction 35%, GPU util +9% (diminishing returns), cost +9%
- Observations: 20m is the sweet spot for most small-burst workloads. 60m shows limited additional latency gain but much higher cost. 5m does not provide meaningful wins for bursty patterns.

Region-specific notes and constraints:
- us-west-2 (pilot): network egress patterns stable. Thermal-throttle alert on node gpu-uw2-34 due to degraded fan firmware. Action: Rajesh to coordinate emergency firmware update and temporary eviction policy for suspicious nodes.
- eu-west-1 (planned expansion): lower baseline demand variability but heavier long-running sessions; potential inefficiency if prewarm profile is too aggressive. Need adjusted predictor thresholds.
- ap-south-1: higher spot variability and longer cold start due to provisioning lag in partner region. Cost sensitivity is higher for customers there. Recommendation: hold off until we can create a "light prewarm" profile that uses smaller instances or container-level warming (KV-only) to reduce resource hold cost.

Operational runbooks / playbook updates (short checklist):
- Prewarm state dashboard (new): created a Grafana panel that shows prewarm slot count, average idle time, recent cold-starts by region. Link in linked_artifacts.
- Eviction policy tweak: if GPU core temp > 78C for >2m, auto-evict prewarm slots and route new requests to on-demand fallback pool. (Temporary threshold until firmware fix.)
- Cost alarm: create an alert when prewarm-cost delta > 6% of region X baseline for 24h. Lina to own alert spec.

Decisions made:
- Expand pilot to eu-west-1 on 2026-03-19 with 20 prewarm slots and TTL=20m; monitor for 72h.
- ap-south expansion postponed; engineering to implement light-profile before scheduling.
- Default TTL for prewarm profiles set to 20m for now; allow per-customer overrides in Dedicated configs.

Actions and owners (clear next steps):
- Rajesh Kumar: firmware patch rollout plan for affected us-west nodes; complete by 2026-03-18. (JIRA-5123)
- Lina Torres: create cost alarm and Grafana dashboard panel, add to infra runbooks; complete by 2026-03-18.
- Ethan Romero: implement eu-west predictor tuning and deployment script for 20-slot expansion; merge PR and smoke test by 2026-03-18 (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/712).
- Sofia Li: prototype light prewarm profile (container-locked KV cache strategy) and cost estimate for ap-south; demo 2026-03-22.
- Maya Patel: runbook update and customer impact note (for CS) describing TTL defaults and opt-outs; draft by 2026-03-17.

Open questions / risks:
- How will prewarming interact with dedicated capacity customers who pin instance types? Need policy to avoid prewarming on reserved nodes unless explicitly allowed. (Config gap: prewarm->reserved mapping.)
- Prediction accuracy: false positives create wasted prewarm slots. Need to instrument per-predictor precision and include feedback loop from actual traffic.
- Billing labeling: clarify whether prewarm idle hours are billed to customer or absorbed by Redwood (policy decision for hosted vs. dedicated). Product to confirm.

Notes from standup exchanges (raw):
- Ethan: "We saw two small regressions in token latency for long sequences when prewarm TTL=60m — suspect cache eviction patterns."
- Rajesh: "Fan firmware is flaky on a subset of older nodes; will isolate and reimage if needed. Noting we should disable prewarming on nodes older than 2024-09 images."
- Lina: "Dashboard is up on staging but needs templating for region variable. Also adding a breakdown by customer tier to spot disproportionately high usage."
- Sofia: "Light prewarm prototype uses a KV-only container that holds cache but not model weights—cost estimate looks promising (~35-40% cheaper card-hour)."

Customer impact and comms plan:
- Minimal immediate customer impact. The TTL default change is internal but will be documented. For Dedicated customers, product will contact customers with pinned capacity before any prewarming on reserved nodes.
- CS notification: send short note explaining improvement in tail latency and the opt-out option for customers worried about prewarm billing. Maya to author.

Follow-ups and milestones:
- 2026-03-18: firmware patch + dashboard + cost alert (owners: Rajesh, Lina).
- 2026-03-19 to 2026-03-22: eu-west pilot expansion monitoring window (owner: Ethan).
- 2026-03-22: ap-south light-profile demo (owner: Sofia).
- 2026-03-24: decision checkpoint to either promote prewarming to default in hosted regions or roll back.

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider a hybrid approach: KV-only prewarm for high-cost regions + full prewarm for core US/EU regions.
- Investigate machine-learning predictor calibration using a rolling 7-day window for better sensitivity to day-of-week patterns.
- Add a cost-forecast line to the Console so customers can preview prewarm-induced variance in expected bill.

Appendix: useful links and logs
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/712
- JIRA: JIRA-5123 (firmware and node eviction), JIRA-5178 (ap-south light-profile)
